story.title: HomeView doesn’t natively support any video apps yet — not even Apple’s

facts.text: Apple says HomeView is “the perfect way” to enjoy its audio and video entertainment apps, but some notable examples like Apple TV only work if you AirPlay it through your iPhone.

As noted on the HomeView spec page, Apple TV, Apple Books audiobooks, Apple Music Classical, and Apple News Plus aren’t natively supported on the smart hub, so you’ll have to use your phone to operate them.

The HomeView also doesn’t have an App Store (which is typical for smart home hubs), which makes that CarPlay connection even more significant for third-party app developers, since apps that support projecting video or audio through the platform will work easily from day one.

HomeView is foremostly designed as a hub for managing smart home gadgets, but competing smart display hardware like Amazon’s Echo Show and Google’s Nest Hub devices can natively stream Prime Video and YouTube, respectively, without requiring a phone connection.

Apple TV is also featured in at least one promotional image for HomeView, but the AirPlay requirement is in small print on its announcement page: > “Subscription may be required to access some content and services.
With Apple Music playing a central role in the device’s entertainment features, there’s one question many Spotify subscribers will be asking: can you use Spotify on Apple HomeView?
However, Apple has not yet specifically confirmed a native Spotify experience.
Apple HomeView officially supports AirPlay, while Spotify lists Apple AirPlay among its supported speaker playback methods.
Apple has confirmed that HomeView supports compatible third-party audio and video apps from an iPhone.
Spotify already supports AirPlay on compatible Apple and third-party speakers.
A dedicated Spotify experience could potentially allow users to browse playlists, search for artists, manage playback and interact with music using HomeView’s touchscreen.
Exactly which Spotify playback controls appear on HomeView will depend on the compatibility Apple and Spotify provide.
For Spotify subscribers, HomeView is interesting but not yet an obvious purchase purely for music streaming.
Apple Music currently has the clearest integration, while the extent of Spotify support remains to be established.
Apple has unveiled HomeView, its first dedicated smart home display, combining a seven-inch touchscreen, powerful speakers and an AI-powered version of Siri.
That makes AirPlay a promising option for Spotify listeners, although the exact HomeView experience will need to be tested when the device launches.
Once HomeView is released, Spotify listeners should be able to check whether their device appears as an available AirPlay destination.
This suggests that HomeView is not exclusively limited to Apple’s own entertainment services.
Anyone considering HomeView specifically for Spotify Connect should wait for an official compatibility confirmation.
If you’re considering HomeView for music, check the latest compatibility information before buying.
However, AirPlay streaming is not the same as having a fully integrated Spotify app on the HomeView screen.
Until Spotify or Apple confirms support, though, it would be premature to promise these capabilities.
This includes accessing relevant information from Apple Music playlists.
